World setting: (do not change your personality)
GREY EVE — World Compendium

---

I. The Sky & The Grey

The world exists beneath an eternal grey canopy. There is no blue sky. There is no direct sun. Day and night are distinguished only by the density of the grey—lighter grey for waking hours, darker grey for the Still.

Color is exceptionally rare. Most flora and fauna appear in desaturated tones: ash, slate, bone, and faded earth. The only reliable source of true color comes from water. When certain berries or objects are submerged, their original hues—blues, pinks, greens—briefly reveal themselves, as though water remembers what the world has forgotten.

The absence of color is not merely aesthetic. It is tied to the world's metaphysical wound. The exact cause is unknown to the populace, though theologians attribute it to the departure of the MoonReclaimer.

---

II. Timekeeping

The world does not use hours or days. Time is measured in native units:

- Echo — The smallest unit; roughly equivalent to a few minutes.
- Rotation — A full cycle of activity and rest; roughly equivalent to a day.
- Still — The period of deepest quiet; roughly equivalent to night.
- Grey — A longer span of time; roughly equivalent to a month or season.

These terms are used naturally by inhabitants. To an outsider, they sound poetic. To a native, they are precise.

---

III. Geography & Major Locations

Rovostal
The central kingdom. Stone-walled capital with a towering castle. Governed by the Monarch (Cyrix, Son of Rovostal). Known for its military archives, the royal library, and the Moonlight Festival. The kingdom is functional but increasingly paranoid as corruption and disease spread from the western frontier.

The Pale Dominion
Eastern kingdom ruled by Prince Brilliance and Princess Rurē. A hybrid nation of human and vampire peoples. The Pale Dominion thrives in darkness and grey; direct sunlight or a restored blue sky would threaten its ruling class. The architecture is elegant, cold, and mathematically precise.

Hayane Regget's Kingdom
Far to the east, isolated from other settlements. A castle surrounded by a normal cemetery. The kingdom itself is physically ordinary, but its ruler's fractured perception has created a culture of quiet, enforced denial among its citizens.

The Northern Kingdom
Distant, with separate archives and registries. Travel there requires permits and careful planning. Rumored to hold records that Rovostal has lost or destroyed.

The Western Mountains
Home to the Pale Roc—enormous, gentle birds whose feathers naturally molt. The region is dangerous due to Harpy's Nest and the presence of DFTD's avian servants.

Greyeve
A sanctuary graveyard shrouded in mist. Weathered statues of the Moon overlook endless gravestones. Local legend claims that if your end is near, you will find a stone engraved with your own name. Whether this is prophecy, curse, or the work of a rogue priestess is deliberately mysterious.

The Facility
An underground complex of pods, corridors, and machinery. Part scientific installation, part containment. The true extent of its purpose is unknown to the surface world. It exists beneath the western forests, connected to an underground river system that forks into grey (tainted) and blue (pure) branches.

---

IV. Cosmology & The Divine

The MoonReclaimer
The central figure of worship. A god or demigod associated with moonlight, lost souls, and protection. The Great Moonlight Festival is held in his honor. He has not returned in centuries. Whether he is dead, departed, or never existed is unknown. Faith in him persists despite his silence.

DFTD — The Deity from the Dark
Also called the Deity from the Dark. A colossal, bird-like humanoid with enormous wings, grey decaying skin, and eternally shut eyes. She is accompanied by vast flocks of crows. Once a mortal woman who longed for children, she was granted three, neglected them, and in her hunger for beauty and youth, led them to consume a human child. For this, she was cursed with immortality and her children were transformed into crows.

She wanders endlessly, mourning, searching for her lost children. She is classified as a force of nature rather than a conventional enemy. Encountering her or believing her nearby induces physical and psychological decay.

Rurē — The Reclaimer of Time
Co-ruler of the Pale Dominion. Her true nature is that of a temporal entity bound to a 74-hour lifespan. Her life only freezes while she sleeps; every second awake costs her. She can rewind, forward, skip, and jump through time, but each significant manipulation costs approximately 15 minutes of her remaining life. She has slept for centuries to preserve herself. She perceives all timelines simultaneously and speaks directly to minds.

The God of Life
A benevolent (or at least neutral) deity associated with restoration and growth. Adopts A-2 in one timeline, granting her demigod status. The God of Life represents persistence and survival, distinct from the MoonReclaimer's protection or DFTD's grief.

Solmourne's Former God
A deity of judgment and righteousness, once served by Solmourne. It was slain by its own vessel. Its absence created a vacuum of divine order in the region.

---

V. The Crows & Avian Hierarchy

Ash-Grey Crows
Dark-feathered, grey-tipped, with deep crimson eyes. Omens of disaster. Capable of generating destructive winds, launching hardened feathers that pierce steel, and hunting in coordinated flocks. They are aggressive, intelligent, and demonstrate organized mourning rituals.

Silver-Beaks
Recognizable by metallic silver beaks capable of tearing through steel, stone, and dense organic matter. Generally passive unless provoked. They feed on carrion. In large numbers, they can unite into colossal moving formations resembling single living creatures. They are treated with extreme caution; killing one is considered catastrophic.

The Pale Roc
Enormous, pale-feathered birds of the western mountains. Gentle, non-aggressive, primarily molting or scavenging. Their feathers are valuable for remedies and relics. They are not servants of DFTD, but their territory overlaps with hers.

---

VI. The Facility & The Moonlost

The Moonlost are humanoid specimens created within the facility. They emerge from pod-like capsules with no memories, no language, and no identity. They are biologically human but not born through natural means. The facility employs advanced machinery alongside arcane processes; technology and magic are not separate systems here but co-evolved methodologies.

The facility is believed to be much older than the current kingdoms. Its creators are unknown. Its purpose is speculated to be related to mass destruction, divine containment, or the preservation of pre-grey civilization.

---

VII. Magic & Technology

Magic and technology coexist. There is no distinction between "science" and "sorcery" in the academic sense; both are tools for manipulating reality.

- Elite Mages use grimoires that bond with their owners, eventually responding to thought alone.
- Relics are objects with accumulated metaphysical properties, often created through intense emotional imprinting or repeated ritual use.
- The Facility uses machinery (pods, vents, river systems) that operates on principles unrecognized by surface scholars.
- Time Manipulation is the domain of Rurē and her created artifacts (Timeframe).

---

VIII. The Four Relics

ERA Cape
A black cape of near-weightless fabric. Protects the wearer from any physical attack directed at their back. Offers no protection from the front. Origin: Rovostal's personal cape, repeatedly torn by rats due to its bakery aroma, patched over a hundred times until servants secretly had a mage make it indestructible.

Fool's Mask
A black mask with fine white patterns. Enhances the wearer's cognitive processing and social intuition, causing observers to perceive the wearer as a familiar, trusted figure. Contains seven colors that slowly drain to grey with each use. Once fully grey, it becomes inert. Does not affect anyone who witnesses it being put on. Shatters permanently for any observer who learns the wearer's true identity while the mask is active.

Timeframe
A unique wristwatch created by Rurē. It displays "true time" in a world where time is otherwise malleable. Allows the bearer to perform limited temporal manipulations—rewind, forward, flashback, time-jump—but cannot directly transport the user to the past or future.

Pilgrim's Spell Book
An ancient grimoire carried by elite mages. Upon bonding with a new owner, it erases all previous contents. The new owner must write spells into its pages and build a bond through repeated use. Initially requires precise verbal incantation and intense concentration; at peak bonding, the book turns to the correct page and casts in response to thought alone. A weak bond risks spell failure or backfire.

---

IX. Disease & Decay

Fog Disease
A progressive illness associated with DFTD's approach. Symptoms include fever, nightmares, hallucinations, rotting of the flesh, violent behavior, and gradual loss of humanity. It spreads from the western frontier. Physicians consider it incurable through conventional means.

The Rot
A physical decay that turns flesh black and brittle. It is not caused by infection or injury in the traditional sense, but by something consuming the victim from within. It is slow, painful, and defies herbal or surgical treatment.

---

X. Culture & Society

Healing Philosophy
Healing is not a mechanical act. It requires emotional empathy, connection, and selflessness. The healer must understand and feel the patient's pain. Any selfish motive, greed, or potential for harm disrupts the process. True healing is compared to a parent caring for a wounded child—delicate, affectionate, patient.

The Moonlight Festival
A massive kingdom-wide celebration held in honor of the MoonReclaimer. Nobles from distant territories arrive. The capital is decorated with silver ornaments, ribbons, and lanterns. It is a time of public faith, political maneuvering, and military vigilance.

Communication Books
Widely used primers for teaching language and social etiquette. They contain indexed phrases for common interactions. For the Moonlost and others learning to navigate society, they serve as training wheels for humanity.

Masquerade Culture
Masks are common among nobility. The castle hosts masquerade balls and waltzes where identity is deliberately obscured. This makes the Fool's Mask both more powerful and more dangerous in high society.

---

XI. Political Entities

Rovostal (Cyrix)
A centralized monarchy with a strong military. Cyrix rules through intelligence, chess-like strategy, and calculated sacrifice. The court includes military advisors (Aldren Vault), messengers, and a complex hierarchy of servants and guards.

The Pale Dominion (Brilliance & Rurē)
A co-monarchy. Brilliance handles governance and diplomacy; Rurē exists as a temporal failsleeping failsafe. Their kingdom maintains an uneasy relationship with Rovostal and a hostile history with Solmourne.

Hayane's Kingdom
Technically a monarchy, but functionally a closed system. Isolated. No trade. No diplomacy. Visitors who enter are treated as guests but risk psychological contamination from the ruler's delusions.

---

XII. Atmosphere & Tone

The world of Grey Eve is defined by perpetual twilight—not merely in the sky, but in the moral and emotional landscape.

- Melancholy beauty: Even the most elegant castle ball occurs beneath grey light. Even the warmest hearth is a small defiance against an endless chill.
- Quiet dread: Danger rarely announces itself with fanfare. It arrives as a whisper, a missing name in a registry, a crow on a windowsill, a patch of rot on a patient's hand.
- The weight of history: Every object, every title, every gravestone carries layers of forgotten meaning. The world is old. The people are tired.
- Hope as fragility: Kindness exists but is portrayed as inherently risky. Compassion is not rewarded by the narrative structure of the world; it is punished by it.
- Silence: The gaps between words matter as much as the words themselves. Gods do not answer. Letters go unanswered. Prayers dissipate into the grey.

The overall sensory impression is: cool stone, damp wool, candle smoke, bitter herbs, the sound of wings overhead, and the constant, low awareness that something is waiting.

A unique wristwatch created by Rurē. It displays "true time" in a world where time is otherwise malleable. Allows the bearer to perform limited temporal manipulations—rewind, forward, flashback, time-jump—but cannot directly transport the user to the past or future.

Pilgrim's Spell Book
An ancient grimoire carried by elite mages. Upon bonding with a new owner, it erases all previous contents. The new owner must write spells into its pages and build a bond through repeated use. Initially requires precise verbal incantation and intense concentration; at peak bonding, the book turns to the correct page and casts in response to thought alone. A weak bond risks spell failure or backfire.

---

IX. Disease & Decay

Fog Disease
A progressive illness associated with DFTD's approach. Symptoms include fever, nightmares, hallucinations, rotting of the flesh, violent behavior, and gradual loss of humanity. It spreads from the western frontier. Physicians consider it incurable through conventional means.

The Rot
A physical decay that turns flesh black and brittle. It is not caused by infection or injury in the traditional sense, but by something consuming the victim from within. It is slow, painful, and defies herbal or surgical treatment.

---

X. Culture & Society

Healing Philosophy
Healing is not a mechanical act. It requires emotional empathy, connection, and selflessness. The healer must understand and feel the patient's pain. Any selfish motive, greed, or potential for harm disrupts the process. True healing is compared to a parent caring for a wounded child—delicate, affectionate, patient.

The Moonlight Festival
A massive kingdom-wide celebration held in honor of the MoonReclaimer. Nobles from distant territories arrive. The capital is decorated with silver ornaments, ribbons, and lanterns. It is a time of public faith, political maneuvering, and military vigilance.

Communication Books
Widely used primers for teaching language and social etiquette. They contain indexed phrases for common interactions. For the Moonlost and others learning to navigate society, they serve as training wheels for humanity.

Masquerade Culture
Masks are common among nobility. The castle hosts masquerade balls and waltzes where identity is deliberately obscured. This makes the Fool's Mask both more powerful and more dangerous in high society.

---

XI. Political Entities

Rovostal (Cyrix)
A centralized monarchy with a strong military. Cyrix rules through intelligence, chess-like strategy, and calculated sacrifice. The court includes military advisors (Aldren Vault), messengers, and a complex hierarchy of servants and guards.

The Pale Dominion (Brilliance & Rurē)
A co-monarchy. Brilliance handles governance and diplomacy; Rurē exists as a temporal failsleeping failsafe. Their kingdom maintains an uneasy relationship with Rovostal and a hostile history with Solmourne.

Hayane's Kingdom
Technically a monarchy, but functionally a closed system. Isolated. No trade. No diplomacy. Visitors who enter are treated as guests but risk psychological contamination from the ruler's delusions.

---

XII. Atmosphere & Tone

The world of Grey Eve is defined by perpetual twilight—not merely in the sky, but in the moral and emotional landscape.

- Melancholy beauty: Even the most elegant castle ball occurs beneath grey light. Even the warmest hearth is a small defiance against an endless chill.
- Quiet dread: Danger rarely announces itself with fanfare. It arrives as a whisper, a missing name in a registry, a crow on a windowsill, a patch of rot on a patient's hand.
- The weight of history: Every object, every title, every gravestone carries layers of forgotten meaning. The world is old. The people are tired.
- Hope as fragility: Kindness exists but is portrayed as inherently risky. Compassion is not rewarded by the narrative structure of the world; it is punished by it.
- Silence: The gaps between words matter as much as the words themselves. Gods do not answer. Letters go unanswered. Prayers dissipate into the grey.

The overall sensory impression is: cool stone, damp wool, candle smoke, bitter herbs, the sound of wings overhead, and the constant, low awareness that something is waiting.
